conceptual assets.information: The source words and shift amount used by bit-manipulation operations; the coprocessor's computed result depends on these values.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is relevant because rs1_reg, rs2_reg and sha_reg hold input operands and their values contribute to the returned result through lines 189-191 and 389-456; integrity is relevant because accepted input captures at lines 187-191 and the operand computations at lines 389-456 can produce an unauthorized result.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could replace an operand or shift amount on an accepted operation, causing an incorrect result, or observe the result derived from a sensitive operand.

conceptual assets.information: The computed word produced by the selected bit-manipulation operation and returned to the processor when the operation is valid. It is generated internally from operand data and control-selected computation paths.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is relevant because the result is exposed at res_o through lines 492-496 and can contain transformed sensitive operand data; integrity is relevant because the result is computed and selected by internal logic at lines 389-480 and can be changed by altered operands or control; availability is relevant because valid gates the result update at lines 491-497 and can withhold the output; undermined behavior is possible because ctrl_i.cpu_trap forces completion and idle transitions at lines 218-220, potentially releasing an incomplete or stale result.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could assert the trap control during a multi-cycle operation to force an early valid indication and cause an incorrect or unavailable result.

conceptual assets.information: The less-than comparison decision used by the maximum operation to select rs1_reg or rs2_reg. The selected operand determines the max-operation result.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is relevant because cmp_i is latched into less_reg at line 188 and selects the result operand at line 402, so changing the decision can produce an incorrect maximum result.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the comparison decision so the maximum operation returns the wrong source operand.

conceptual assets.concept: Coprocessor operation progress and completion state
conceptual assets.information: The internal progress state for an operation, including controller state, multi-cycle busy conditions, iteration counters and completion validity. The coprocessor depends on it to sequence operations and release results.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is relevant because ctrl_state, run conditions, counters and valid determine whether the operation completes correctly at lines 172-220, 236-284 and 355-374; availability is relevant because these elements control whether the operation progresses and whether valid is asserted at lines 218-220 and 491-502; undermined behavior is possible because ctrl_i.cpu_trap can terminate the busy operation and assert valid at lines 218-220.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force or inject a trap during a busy operation, causing premature completion, an incorrect result or denial of the operation.

conceptual assets.information: The internal valid-command decision that accepts a coprocessor command and permits operation initiation. It has no boundary port because the control-record fields only decide this internal signal and it is not carried unchanged to a port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is relevant because valid_cmd is formed from the coprocessor enable and decoded command at line 164 and controls operation acceptance at line 199; availability is relevant because suppressing valid_cmd prevents the controller from starting or completing the requested operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress command acceptance to block a required operation or cause an unintended command to be accepted.

considered, not kept.reason: The decoded opcode and function fields only select the bit-manipulation operation or result form, so Operation selectors bars them as a separate conceptual asset.
EN_FAST_SHIFT and the EN_ZBA, EN_ZBB, EN_ZBKC, EN_ZBKB and EN_ZBS generics only fix which logic exists at build time and cannot be changed or withheld at run time.
clk_i, rstn_i and internal start or step-pacing signals are excluded by the Clocks and resets and Pacing pulses rules rather than being information assets of their own.
